text:
vp-eng: Short post-all-hands thread 1 Need two crisp answers for the release page: 1) What's the hosted p95 target next quarter? 2) How will we rollback kernel/batching/cache changes (short bullets)? @maya-eng-runtime @alex-eng-sre

maya-eng-runtime: Hosted target = p95 token latency <200ms for standard tier. Dedicated target = p95 <150ms under committed load. Rollouts are staged canaries (small -> medium -> full). Kernels are independent infra changes; batching/cache are workload-layer and usually follow kernels to exploit perf gains.

alex-eng-sre: Rollback bullets: auto-rollback if p95 increases by >9% vs baseline OR absolute error-rate increase >0.4% sustained for 30m; immediate rollback on new OOMs or GPU resets. Canary step min = 24h unless traffic is very stable. We'll run shadow traffic for correctness diffs.

jamal-ml: ML note: kernel changes can change optimal batch sizes and memory footprint. We'll publish a short table mapping model families to expected perf delta and recommended batching after kernel canary.

nina-product: Product ask: will Dedicated customers be forced into rollouts? Need one-liner for the console modal.

maya-eng-runtime: One-liner: "Dedicated customers can pin a model variant per route to prevent automatic runtime updates." We'll add a small explainer: pinning freezes kernels, batching and cache for that route.

sam-cs: CS question: if prewarm runs during canary, does that count against committed throughput? Short answer please.

jamal-ml: Short: prewarm counts as normal inference traffic. For Dedicated, prewarm can be isolated into a background pool on request to avoid consuming committed spikes.

ops-bot: scheduled: attn-tiling-canary -> 2025-06-16 02:00 UTC (initial window 48h) Monitor: https://console.redwood.ai/mon/attn-tiling-canary

vp-eng: Nice. Action items: eng-runtime publish the rollout summary + model-family table by EOD Fri; eng-sre add the auto-rollback monitors and runbook; product + CS prepare console copy and CS FAQ. Ping me on PRs. :raised_hands:
